title: Time-domain FI/SCA jitter at the NSC boundary: glitch-detecting wait_random at veneer entry/exit plus a per-NSC-call 'session delay' re-sample (Trezor RDI)
threat: The NSC call is the one host-visible phase marker: a host that times its own HID frame can align a glitch (clock/voltage/EM) or power/EM trace on the secure handler's first instructions — the PIN-verified sentinel read, pointer validation, entry_point compare, sender binding — with cycle-stable offsets. pq1 has double-compute/CFI on signing and a power-domain consumption mask (dilution unmeasured), but nothing in the time domain between NS->S entry and the first sentinel check.
proposal: (1) Call `fi::wait_random()` (the existing pqsigner-fi double-counter loop that halts on `i+j != wait`) as the first statement of every veneer after the USB-01 try-enter and immediately before each veneer's return. (2) Add a Trezor-style RDI: the S-only 1 ms tick (TIM2 or SysTick) busy-waits `drbg_byte() + session_delay` cycles; `session_delay` is re-sampled on every NSC entry and on every trusted-UI button event (the two host-visible phase markers). Source bytes from `rng_strong` with a budget so the #802 SysTick-entropy drain is not worsened (use a ChaCha DRBG reseeded from TRNG, as Trezor does, and make lock-contention a hard error rather than a constant). (3) Measure the added latency with `make test-key-speed` and pin the new baselines.
rationale: The primitive already exists and is proven glitch-detecting (pqsigner-fi/src/lib.rs:129-155) but is wired only around the crypto verify; threat-model.md:321 lists the sentinel as 'Planned'. Random per-call jitter forces a glitcher to search a window instead of hitting an offset, and the session term defeats averaging across calls. Cheap, orthogonal to the consumption mask, and lands on the exact boundary that the host controls.
repo_evidence: secure/src/fi.rs:7-9 (wait_random re-exported; grep shows callers only in crypto.rs:352,407 and fih.rs:114 — none at NSC entry)
secure/src/nsc/mod.rs:1923-1960 (veneers: secure_log then straight into cmd::run)
secure/src/main.rs:4343-4361 (#802: SysTick already draws TRNG per ms when idle — budget interaction)
vendor_precedent: Trezor random_delays.c:139-162 (1 ms RDI timer, session delay refreshed on USB in/out) and :189-202 (wait_random with i+j invariant -> error_shutdown('(glitch)')); usb.c inserts wait_random before each control-request branch and usb_class_hid.c:337 on every OUT packet.
risks: Adds ~hundreds of cycles per NSC call and a 1 ms handler (Trezor's cost is accepted); must not touch the consumption mask's TIM; entropy budget vs #802; test-key-speed baselines change; the RDI must be disabled during the SE I2C timing-critical windows (OPTIGA 50 us guard time) or run at a priority that cannot stretch them.
sources: Clavier/Coron/Dabbous 'Differential power analysis in the presence of hardware countermeasures' (CHES 2000) — floating-mean random delays
